label: One-sided third-factor bound on wrongly endorsed acts
description: The strongest quantified form of Enoch's modest correlation available from his one-direction premise: what selection disposes us to endorse is mostly backed by a reason, with wrongly endorsed acts at most d1 + d2, and no independence assumed. It uses only the factor-without-reason direction the pro tanto goodness of survival bears on, and says nothing about reasons B fails to endorse. Both rates are open inputs; nothing is derived about their values.
